note: Read tools execute immediately; run_workflow creates a confirmation ticket. Multi-hop capped by BACKEND_AGENT_MAX_TOOL_HOPS. web_search gated by BACKEND_AGENT_WEB_SEARCH_ENABLED. list_workflow_timers is admin-only.

tools.name: search_layers
tools.description: Search layers by keyword (read-only, ACL filtered). Results also include the layers currently loaded on the user's page (client_context.active_layers), which are usually NOT in the catalog; such hits come first and carry on_page=true, visible, selected, layer_kind (runtime_product = a materialized run product, catalog_reference = a catalog entry) and product_class (derived_product = local inversion/materialized product, reference_layer = reference/official layer shipped with the catalog, catalog_other). When the user only names a data source (SMAP, FengYun, L3), treat it as the SOURCE, not the layer: prefer on_page/visible/selected hits over catalog references, never silently substitute a catalog reference layer for the layer the user is actually looking at, and if the only candidates differ by product_class (derived_product vs reference_layer) ask the user which one they mean instead of picking one.

tools.name: list_workflows
tools.description: List available workflow definitions/templates (read-only). Optional keyword filter.

query.description: Optional keyword matched against workflow id/name/tags

tools.name: get_layer_meta
tools.description: Get detailed metadata for one layer (read-only, ACL filtered): description, readiness, extent, workflow binding, tags, plus temporal facts. temporal_coverage and declared_temporal_coverage are only the descriptor CLAIM; actual_temporal_coverage / actual_block_count / actual_time_blocks / temporal_summary come from the real time_list on disk. When coverage_conflict=true the claim contradicts the product, so trust actual_* and never quote the declared dates.

tools.name: get_workflow_meta
tools.description: Get detailed info for one workflow definition (read-only, ACL): description, engine, node summary, linked layer.

tools.name: sample_layer_point
tools.description: Sample raster/overlay (or weather) value at a map point. Uses args lng/lat, or client_context.map_point if omitted. Optional catalog_id; otherwise samples active layers from client_context. Each overlay sample returns requested_time plus actual_time / period_start / period_end, so report the data time block per layer instead of reusing one layer's period for another.

catalog_id.description: Optional single layer; if omitted sample active layers

time.description: Optional time key (e.g. YYYYMMDD) for time-series overlays

tools.name: web_search
tools.description: Search the public web (DuckDuckGo Instant Answer + Wikipedia fallback) for background knowledge. Not for private/intranet data.

tools.name: list_workflow_runs
tools.description: List recent workflow runs for the current user (admin sees all). Filter by status / active_only / limit.

status.description: Optional status filter e.g. succeeded / failed / running

tools.name: get_workflow_run
tools.description: Get status of one workflow run by run_id (owner-scoped).

tools.name: get_layer_coverage
tools.description: Get dual-channel data coverage for a catalog layer (online window + local dates). Pass `time` to get a decisive answer (`resolved.status` = available/unavailable) about whether that date has data, and `resolved.channel` to tell local products apart from online fetching. The TOP-LEVEL `actual_time` is the authoritative hit and may be a single day produced on demand from NAS that is NOT in time_list: `hit_source=ondemand_frame` means it really is that day's own observation (`is_daily_frame=true`), while `hit_source=block` means the date merely falls inside a multi-day block. Always prefer top-level `actual_time` over `resolved.actual_time` (which only reflects time_list blocks). `available_dates` lists the real neighbouring dates on that layer (first/last/count plus before/after around `time`): when a date has no data, the ONLY dates you may suggest come from there, and you must say they are the dates this layer actually has. Never infer or invent a substitute date.

time.description: Optional date to resolve, e.g. 20251215 or 2025-12-15

tools.name: get_layer_statistics
tools.description: Read-only raster statistics for one local imported layer at one time slice: mean/min/max/std and valid pixel count, NoData excluded. Both catalog_id and time are optional: when omitted, catalog_id falls back to the selected/visible runtime layer in client_context.active_layers, and time falls back to client_context.timeline.date (the page's current date) - so 'the current layer' really means what the user is looking at. The response carries time_source telling where the date came from: page / requested / layer_default (layer_default means it is NOT the page's date and you must say so). period_start~period_end is the time block actually hit; layer_span_start~layer_span_end is the whole layer's span - never mix them. is_daily_frame tells whether this is a single-day observation. Scope defaults to the full raster extent (never the current viewport); pass bbox only when the user explicitly asks for a sub-area. Never creates layers, never writes products, never runs a workflow. Also returns extent (WGS84 bbox actually analyzed) and temporal_summary.

time.description: Optional date, e.g. 20251215 or 2025-12-15; omit to use the layer default time

bbox.description: Optional WGS84 bounding box [west, south, east, north] in degrees. Omit for the whole raster. Only pass when the user names an area.

tools.name: list_workflow_timers
tools.description: List workflow timers (admin only). Optional workflow_id filter.

tools.name: run_workflow
tools.description: Prepare a workflow-run for a catalog layer. Does NOT submit until the user confirms via confirmation card. Optional time_range (ISO start/end) and workflow_variant=online.

workflow_id.description: Optional workflow seed id; defaults to layer descriptor workflow_id

workflow_variant.description: Use online variant seed when declared on the layer
